questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.03

A team is publishing a digital flyer for students about lunch pre-order forms. Which element is most necessary for a clear multimedia publication?

answer.text: A. Several unrelated images and very little text.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Visuals must support the message instead of replacing it.

answer.text: B. A focused message, accurate evidence, and a visual that helps students understand the point.

feedback.text: Correct. A multimedia publication should combine text, evidence, and visual support for the intended audience.

answer.text: C. A complete copied research report.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A flyer should select and adapt evidence for the audience.

answer.text: D. A message written only for adults.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The assigned audience is students.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.04

Which sentence is best revised for a student audience?

answer.text: A. Students must comply with institutional meal-planning procedures.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is formal and distant for a student flyer.

answer.text: B. Food logistics are a problem of operational concern.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too abstract for the purpose.

answer.text: C. Meal allocation systems require procedural alignment.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is unnecessarily complex.

answer.text: D. When students complete the pre-order form, staff can prepare meals students are more likely to choose.

feedback.text: Correct. This is clear, accurate, and audience-appropriate.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.03

Which visual choice best supports a flyer about reducing unwanted trays?

answer.text: A. A labeled chart showing fewer unwanted trays after the pre-order pilot.

feedback.text: Correct. The chart directly supports the central research finding.

answer.text: B. A photo of a school hallway.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The image does not connect to the lunch-form message.

answer.text: C. A decorative border with no evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration does not help the audience understand the finding.

answer.text: D. A random clip art image of a notebook.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This visual is unrelated to the topic.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which presentation plan best shows collaborative preparation?

answer.text: A. One speaker handles every part because it is faster.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Collaboration requires shared responsibility.

answer.text: B. Each speaker gives a different unsupported opinion.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presentation should stay focused on the evidence-based plan.

answer.text: C. One speaker explains audience, one explains evidence, one explains visual design, and one explains revision choices.

feedback.text: Correct. Clear roles help the group present a unified multimedia plan.

answer.text: D. Speakers repeat the same point without roles.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Repetition does not show purposeful collaboration.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.03

Which wording best combines evidence and voice for an expository publication?

answer.text: A. The pilot report found fewer unwanted trays after students used pre-order forms, which shows how one small routine can reduce waste.

feedback.text: Correct. The sentence integrates evidence and explains its significance in a clear voice.

answer.text: B. The forms were awesome and fixed everything.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is exaggerated and informal.

answer.text: C. There was a report and some trays.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and does not explain the evidence.

answer.text: D. Waste is bad, obviously.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is opinion without source support.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.03

A team wants its flyer to be easy to scan. Which design decision best supports that goal?

answer.text: A. Use one long paragraph with no headings.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A long block of text is difficult to scan.

answer.text: B. Use tiny text so more information fits.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Tiny text makes the publication harder to read.

answer.text: C. Use five different unrelated fonts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Too many fonts distract from the message.

answer.text: D. Use a short headline, brief evidence statement, labeled visual, and clear call to action.

feedback.text: Correct. These elements help students quickly understand the message.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.04

Which revision most improves audience awareness?

answer.text: A. "Pre-order compliance is administratively beneficial."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too formal and unclear for students.

answer.text: B. "Filling out the form helps the cafeteria prepare meals students actually choose."

feedback.text: Correct. This revision explains the benefit in clear student-friendly language.

answer.text: C. "The food thing works if people do it."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague and informal.

answer.text: D. "Procedural forms must be submitted by all."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is formal and rule-focused.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.03

Which statement best explains why a visual should be included?

answer.text: A. A visual should be included because every assignment needs a picture.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Visuals should have a purpose, not just be added automatically.

answer.text: B. A visual should replace all written explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Multimedia publication uses visual and written elements together.

answer.text: C. A visual should make the research finding easier to understand for the intended audience.

feedback.text: Correct. The visual must support comprehension of the message.

answer.text: D. A visual should be unrelated so it looks interesting.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unrelated visuals weaken the publication.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

A group member disagrees with the chosen visual. Which response best supports productive collaboration?

answer.text: A. Ignore the concern and submit the first design.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Ignoring feedback weakens collaboration.

answer.text: B. Remove all visuals to avoid disagreement.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The assignment requires multimedia publication.

answer.text: C. Let the loudest member decide without discussion.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Collaboration requires reasoned decision-making.

answer.text: D. Ask the member to explain how another visual might better support the audience and evidence.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the discussion focused on purpose and evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.03

Which sentence best explains the significance of the evidence?

answer.text: A. The finding matters because it shows that student choices can help staff prepare fewer unwanted meals.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains why the evidence matters to the audience and purpose.

answer.text: B. The evidence is there because the report had information.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain significance.

answer.text: C. The report is probably useful.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is uncertain and vague.

answer.text: D. Forms are used in schools.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This fact does not explain the lesson's research finding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.03

Which publication choice would most likely confuse the student audience?

answer.text: A. A clear headline about completing the pre-order form.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A clear headline supports understanding.

answer.text: B. A labeled chart connected to the research finding.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This helps the audience interpret evidence.

answer.text: C. A technical paragraph full of cafeteria management terms without explanation.

feedback.text: Correct. Unexplained technical language can confuse the intended audience.

answer.text: D. A short action step telling students what to do next.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A clear action step supports the purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.04

Which revision keeps the meaning but improves clarity?

answer.text: A. "The form situation was handled."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: B. "Pre-ordering helps staff prepare meals based on what students choose."

feedback.text: Correct. This revision is clear and keeps the original meaning.

answer.text: C. "Pre-ordering impacts operational tray outcomes."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unnecessarily complex.

answer.text: D. "Do it because forms matter."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain the benefit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which oral explanation best supports the team's visual choice?

answer.text: A. "We chose a before-and-after chart because it directly shows the change in unwanted trays after the pilot."

feedback.text: Correct. This explanation connects the visual to evidence and purpose.

answer.text: B. "We chose the chart because it looked cool."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain how the visual supports the message.

answer.text: C. "We did not think about the visual much."

feedback.text: Incorrect. The publication should use purposeful design.

answer.text: D. "The visual does not really connect, but it fills space."

feedback.text: Incorrect. A visual should not be filler.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.03

Which detail should be removed from a student flyer?

answer.text: A. A short explanation of why the form matters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This supports the purpose.

answer.text: B. A labeled visual showing the research finding.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This supports understanding.

answer.text: C. A clear student action step.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This helps the audience know what to do.

answer.text: D. An unrelated paragraph about school parking rules.

feedback.text: Correct. Unrelated information distracts from the publication's message.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.03

Which sentence uses an appropriate academic voice for the flyer?

answer.text: A. The lunch form thing is kind of useful or whatever.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and vague.

answer.text: B. Students are the only reason waste happens.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is blaming and unsupported.

answer.text: C. Completing the form can help the cafeteria prepare meals that better match student choices.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence is clear, accurate, and respectful.

answer.text: D. Everyone better submit the form now.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is demanding rather than informative.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.04

Which question should a team ask during revision?

answer.text: A. Can we make the flyer longer even if students stop reading?

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length alone does not improve communication.

answer.text: B. Will students understand the message, evidence, visual, and action step quickly?

feedback.text: Correct. This question checks audience awareness and clarity.

answer.text: C. Can we add unrelated details to fill space?

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unrelated details weaken focus.

answer.text: D. Can we use more difficult words to sound advanced?

feedback.text: Incorrect. Audience-aware revision values clarity.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.03

Which choice best combines written and visual information?

answer.text: A. A chart appears with no label or explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience may not understand what the chart shows.

answer.text: B. A paragraph explains the finding while the image shows an unrelated sports logo.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The visual does not support the text.

answer.text: C. A sentence explains the pilot finding, and a chart displays the change in unwanted trays.

feedback.text: Correct. The text and visual work together to teach the same message.

answer.text: D. A decorative background replaces all evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration cannot replace evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which team role is most directly responsible for checking that the flyer is accurate?

answer.text: A. Evidence reviewer.

feedback.text: Correct. This role checks that claims match the source findings.

answer.text: B. Person who chooses colors only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Color choice matters, but accuracy requires checking claims and evidence.

answer.text: C. Person who counts words only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Word count does not confirm accuracy.

answer.text: D. Person who ignores the source.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Accuracy depends on using the source correctly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.03

Which sentence should be revised because it overstates the evidence?

answer.text: A. The pilot report found fewer unwanted trays after the pre-order process.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This accurately states the finding.

answer.text: B. Pre-order forms will completely eliminate all cafeteria waste forever.

feedback.text: Correct. This overstates what the evidence can prove.

answer.text: C. Reminders can help more students complete the form.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a reasonable statement from the lesson evidence.

answer.text: D. The flyer should explain how the form connects to meal preparation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is accurate and relevant.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.04

Which call to action best fits the student audience?

answer.text: A. Fulfill institutional submission procedures immediately.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too formal and unclear.

answer.text: B. The cafeteria thanks stakeholders for compliance.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is adult-centered and distant.

answer.text: C. Pre-order processes should be operationalized.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unclear for students.

answer.text: D. Complete the lunch form when it opens so staff can prepare meals students are more likely to choose.

feedback.text: Correct. This is clear, specific, and connected to the evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.03

Which item belongs in the final publication checklist?

answer.text: A. The visual supports the evidence instead of distracting from it.

feedback.text: Correct. Purposeful visuals are required for effective multimedia publication.

answer.text: B. The flyer includes every fact the team found.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The team should select the most relevant evidence.

answer.text: C. The design hides the source finding.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The evidence should be easy to find.

answer.text: D. The message changes depending on who reads it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The message should stay focused and clear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.03

Which source integration is strongest?

answer.text: A. A report says things happened.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague to support the message.

answer.text: B. People talked about lunch a lot.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not integrate research evidence.

answer.text: C. The pilot report found that unwanted trays decreased after staff prepared meals from student selections.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence clearly identifies the source and finding.

answer.text: D. It was good because it was good.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is circular and unsupported.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which group explanation best shows the connection between purpose and audience?

answer.text: A. We made the flyer because the assignment said to.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain audience or purpose.

answer.text: B. We used random images so students would notice them.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Attention alone is not enough if the images do not support the message.

answer.text: C. We wrote it in the longest way possible.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Long wording may reduce clarity.

answer.text: D. We wanted students to understand that completing the form can help reduce unwanted trays, so we used simple wording and a clear chart.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects audience, purpose, wording, and visual design.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.04

Which sentence needs revision because it is not audience-aware?

answer.text: A. Completing the form helps staff prepare meals students are more likely to choose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is student-friendly and clear.

answer.text: B. Stakeholders must enact compliance with food-service optimization protocols.

feedback.text: Correct. This language is too formal and unclear for the student audience.

answer.text: C. A short reminder can help students remember to submit the form.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is clear and relevant.

answer.text: D. The flyer should explain the benefit in simple language.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This shows audience awareness.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_L06_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.03

Which final product best meets the lesson goal?

answer.text: A. A student-facing digital flyer with a clear headline, accurate evidence, labeled visual, and specific action step.

feedback.text: Correct. This product combines collaboration, audience awareness, evidence, and multimedia publication.

answer.text: B. A private group note with no visual and no audience plan.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not meet the multimedia publication goal.

answer.text: C. A long copied report without revision.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not adapted for the student audience.

answer.text: D. An unrelated slideshow about another school issue.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not match the lesson focus or standards.
